dark.description: Dark theme: over `#191817`, `#201F1D`, `#2A2826`, `#121110`, `#24221F`, and the made `accentSubtle`.

light.description: Light theme: over `#FFFFFF`, `#F7F6F3`, `#F1F0ED`, `#F4F3F0`, and the made `accentSubtle`.

acceptable.description: Both contrasts are 4.5 or more, so `updateBranding` takes the color (S9-AC-11).

password.description: 10 to 72 characters, not only whitespace, not the same as the email (AUTH-5).

token.description: The token from the invitation link's fragment (after `#`). Sent only in the body.

anonymized.description: The account was anonymized (PII-4): `name` and `email` are the anonymous values, `status` is `SUSPENDED`, and nothing brings it back (S10A-AC-13).

oidcLinked.description: The account is linked to an OIDC provider's account (AUTH-6, S11-AC-26): later OIDC sign-ins match it by that link only. `unlinkAccountOidc` removes it.

photoUpdatedAt.description: When the profile photo last changed; null without a photo (`getPhoto`).

attachments.description: Files the account uploaded and did not delete, without their content; temporary images not attached yet are left out (S10A-AC-04). Oldest first (`createdAt`, then ID).

comments.description: Comments the account wrote and did not delete, internal ones included, on issues that are not purged (S10A-AC-03). Oldest first (`createdAt`, then ID).

issues.description: Issues the account is the reporter of, filed on its behalf included; not the ones it filed for someone else. Issues in the trash are in it, purged ones are not (S10A-AC-02). Oldest first (`createdAt`, then ID).

photo.description: Null without a profile photo, and for an anonymized account (S10A-AC-07).

name.description: The anonymous name for an anonymized account.

commentId.description: The comment it belongs to; null for a file on the issue itself.

deletedAt.description: When it went into the trash; null when it is not there.

base64.description: The PNG file, Base64 (RFC 4648, with padding, no line breaks).

ApiError.description: Error body. Clients choose the text they show by `code`; `message` is a default text for a `code` they do not know.

brokenSeq.description: Present only when the audit log's hash chain is broken (409 `AUDIT_CHAIN_BROKEN`, S10A-AC-37): the `seq` of the first entry that does not hold.

code.description: Stable error key. See docs/integrate/conventions.md for the list.

fields.description: Present only when the error is about specific fields (400 `INVALID_INPUT`).

issueKeys.description: Present only when the error is about other issues: the keys of the other issues whose links stop a restore (409 `RESTORE_LINK_CONFLICT`, S7A-AC-24).

commentId.description: The comment it belongs to; null for a file on the issue itself.

fileName.description: Cleared to null when the attachment is deleted (COM-7, ATT-5).

id.description: Hard to guess, but not a permission check (ATT-7).

inline.description: A content image: uploaded with `uploadImage` and attached through `imageIds` of a save, to be shown in the content as `![…](attachment:{id})`. Listed, downloaded, and deleted like every other attachment (S5-AC-24).

accountId.description: 0 for popdesk itself (the first admin, commands in the container).

action.description: The kind of action as the entry holds it now; it may be a changed value.
The kind of action: a value of the `action` filter. An entry someone changed in the database may hold another name, so this is a plain string.

changes.description: What changed, as stored. A changed value is `{"from": ..., "to": ...}` under its field name; a value set for the first time is the value itself. Null when the action changes no value. A sign-in by OIDC (`SIGN_IN_SUCCEEDED`, `SIGN_IN_FAILED`) and an invitation accepted by it (`INVITATION_ACCEPTED`) have `{"method": "OIDC"}`; a password sign-in has none. `OIDC_LINKED` has `issuer`, the provider's `iss`; never the `sub` (S11-AC-24).

hash.description: SHA-256 of `prevHash` and the entry's canonical JSON: 64 lowercase hex characters.

occurredAt.description: When the action was done, with microseconds.

prevHash.description: The `hash` of the entry before this one in the chain; 64 zeros for the first.

seq.description: The entry's place in the hash chain, from 1.

target.description: What the action was done to, as stored: `type` (`ACCOUNT`, `COMPANY`, `DATABASE`, `AUDIT_LOG`, `SLA_POLICY`, `BRANDING`) and the keys that name it (`accountId`, `code`). An issue deleted, restored, or purged by an admin (`ISSUE_DELETED`, `ISSUE_RESTORED`, `ISSUE_PURGED`) is `{"type": "COMPANY", "code": …, "issueKey": …}`, with the issue's company and key and never its title, and `changes` is null (S7A-AC-07). A change of the SLA policy (`SLA_POLICY_CHANGED`) is `{"type": "SLA_POLICY", "version": …}` with the new version (S8A-AC-06). A change of the display name or the accent color (`BRANDING_CHANGED`) is `{"type": "BRANDING"}` (S9-AC-20); a new or removed logo (`BRANDING_LOGO_CHANGED`) is `{"type": "BRANDING", "theme": …}` with `LIGHT` or `DARK` (S9-AC-21). An account export or anonymization (`ACCOUNT_EXPORTED`, `ACCOUNT_ANONYMIZED`) is `{"type": "ACCOUNT", "accountId": …}`; the chain computed again after an anonymization (`AUDIT_RECHAINED`) is `{"type": "AUDIT_LOG"}` (S10A-AC-06, S10A-AC-16, S10A-AC-18). A company export asked for or downloaded (`COMPANY_EXPORTED`, `COMPANY_EXPORT_DOWNLOADED`) is `{"type": "COMPANY", "code": …}` (S10B-AC-09). An OIDC link made, removed, or an invitation accepted by an OIDC sign-in (`OIDC_LINKED`, `OIDC_UNLINKED`, `INVITATION_ACCEPTED`) is `{"type": "ACCOUNT", "accountId": …}` (S11-AC-24, S11-AC-27).

brokenEntry.description: The first entry that does not hold. Null when `valid`, and for `HEAD_MISMATCH`, where no entry that is left is wrong.

checkedCount.description: Entries whose hash was computed again and matched.

valid.description: Every entry and the end of the chain hold.

accent.description: The accent color as saved, `#RRGGBB` in capitals; null for the app's own colors.

colors.description: The values made from `accent`; null without one.

contrast.description: The contrast of `colors`; null without an accent color.

version.description: Goes up by 1 when the display name or the accent color changes, not when a logo does (S9-AC-18). Send it back with `updateBranding`.

url.description: Its public address, `/api/public/branding/logos/{theme}?v={fingerprint}`, the same as in `getPublicBranding`.

dark.description: Null without a logo for the dark theme.

light.description: Null without a logo for the light theme.

newPassword.description: 10 to 72 characters, not only whitespace, not the same as the email (AUTH-5).

holidays.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, in any order, at most 500, no day twice; popdesk keeps them earliest first.

hours.description: Seven items, one for each weekday, in any order. `opens` and `closes` both null for a day without business hours.

targets.description: Four items, one for each priority, in any order. A goal left null is no goal.

version.description: The `version` of the policy as the caller read it (S8A-AC-03).

enabled.description: Configured, and not turned off by the sandbox (S4B-AC-08).

deleted.description: How many rows that run deleted; null when the job never ran.

lastRunAt.description: When the job last ran; null when it never ran.

name.description: The job's name, as in the metrics label `job`, for example `session-cleanup`.

issues.description: Issues whose assignee was cleared. 0 without `clearAssignments`.

content.description: Markdown, as written (COM-6). An empty string once the comment is deleted (COM-7).

editedAt.description: When the author last changed the content; null when it never changed (S4-AC-07).

internal.description: Internal comments do not exist for customers (CMT-2).

mentions.description: The accounts the comment mentions, as they were chosen: someone who can no longer see the issue stays in the list (S4-AC-19, S4-AC-26). In name order, then by account ID.

code.description: 2 to 10 capital letters and digits. Unique, never changes.

pendingMembershipRequests.description: Membership requests for this company that wait for an admin (S2-AC-48).

failure.description: Why a `FAILED` export stopped; null for the other states.

finishedAt.description: When the export became `DONE` or `FAILED`; null while it is `RUNNING`. An `EXPIRED` export keeps the time it became `DONE`.

includeInternal.description: Internal comments and tasks are in the ZIP (S10B-AC-13).

includePrivate.description: Private issues are in the ZIP (S10B-AC-16).

size.description: Bytes of the ZIP; null unless the export became `DONE`.

state.description: A `DONE` export whose ZIP is over 24 hours old is `EXPIRED`, even before the cleanup job deletes the file (S10B-AC-03).

anonymized.description: The account was anonymized (PII-4): `name` and `email` are the anonymous values and `status` is `SUSPENDED` (B2-AC-01). `false` for every other account.

manager.description: The customer is a manager of this company (MGR-1). Always `false` for an agent.

photoUpdatedAt.description: When the profile photo last changed; null without a photo (`getPhoto`).
When the profile photo last changed; null without a photo (`getPhoto`).

companyStatus.description: The company's status now; archived companies are listed too.

sla.description: The SLA goals over the chosen `days`, counted from the same issues the caller can see. Null while the SLA policy is off; in one answer every item is null or none is (S8B-AC-22). The counts above do not depend on `days` (S8B-AC-21).

total.description: Every issue, in any status; the sum of the four counts below.

items.description: One item per company: by `open`, the most first, then by `companyCode`. Empty when the caller can see no company.

imageIds.description: IDs of temporary images the caller uploaded with `uploadImage`, up to 20. The save attaches them to the issue, and to the comment when it writes one, or attaches none of them and saves nothing (S5-AC-20). Only these IDs are attached: the server does not look for `attachment:{id}` in the content, and an ID the content does not name is attached too (S5-AC-25). An ID given twice counts once. Left out, `null`, or empty: nothing is attached.

internal.description: An internal comment, hidden from customers. Public when left out.

mentions.description: Account IDs to mention, up to 10, each one of `listMentionCandidates` for this kind of comment (MNT-1). An ID given twice counts once. Left out is the same as an empty list.

includeInternal.description: Also put internal comments and tasks in the ZIP, with the attachments of those comments (S10B-AC-13, S10B-AC-14).

includePrivate.description: Also put private issues in the ZIP: issues other customers of the same company cannot see either (S10B-AC-16).

code.description: 2 to 10 capital letters and digits, unique. Cannot be changed later.

companyCodes.description: Codes of the companies a customer joins. At least one for `CUSTOMER`; left out or empty for staff.

issueKey.description: Key of the other issue. Missing, `null`, or empty after the whitespace around it is removed is `REQUIRED`; a key the caller cannot see, or a value that is not a key, is 404 (S6C-AC-02, S6C-AC-03).

type.description: Seen from this issue (S6C-AC-13): `DUPLICATE_OF` makes this issue a duplicate of the other one, `DUPLICATED_BY` the other one a duplicate of this one. Missing or `null` is `REQUIRED`, any other value `UNKNOWN_VALUE`.

companyCode.description: Code of an active company the caller can see.

content.description: Markdown, up to 10,000 characters. Empty when left out.

imageIds.description: IDs of temporary images the caller uploaded with `uploadImage`, up to 20. The save attaches them to the issue, and to the comment when it writes one, or attaches none of them and saves nothing (S5-AC-20). Only these IDs are attached: the server does not look for `attachment:{id}` in the content, and an ID the content does not name is attached too (S5-AC-25). An ID given twice counts once. Left out, `null`, or empty: nothing is attached.

reporterId.description: Account ID of an `ACTIVE` customer who belongs to that company. The customer is the reporter of the issue.

color.description: `#` and six hexadecimal digits; small letters are stored as capitals (S6A-AC-04). Left out or `null`: `#808080`.

name.description: 1 to 30 characters after the whitespace around it is removed and the text is put in Unicode NFC. Unique in the company whatever the case (S6A-AC-02, S6A-AC-03).

assigneeId.description: An `ACTIVE` admin, or an `ACTIVE` agent assigned to the issue's company, as for the issue's assignee (TASK-6, S6B-AC-04). Left out or `null`: nobody.

dueDate.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, today or later in the installation time zone, by the rules of the issue's due date (S6B-AC-05). Left out or `null`: none.

title.description: 1 to 100 characters after the whitespace around it is removed (S6B-AC-02).

auditEntryId.description: The audit entry of an outside copy (`AUDIT_FORWARD`); null for the other channels.

lastErrorKind.description: Kind of the last error, for example `CONNECTION_FAILED`, or `RATE_LIMITED` for an email over the 50 an hour one address gets (S4B-AC-10); never the error text.

recipientAccountId.description: The receiving account of an email; null for a webhook.

code.description: Stable field error key, for example `TOO_LONG`.

field.description: Name of the request field or query parameter.

inviteLink.description: Shown once; the token is in the fragment after `#`.
The invitation link, only when SMTP is not configured; shown once. `null` when the invitation email is sent.

assigneeUnavailable.description: The assignee can no longer see the issue: the account is not `ACTIVE`, or it is an agent who is not assigned to the company (ISSUE-11). `false` without an assignee.

closedAt.description: When the issue became `CLOSED`; null while it is open.

createdBy.description: The staff member who filed the issue for the reporter; null when the reporter filed it (S3-AC-36).

labels.description: Labels of the issue, at most 20, in name order whatever the case (S6A-AC-50). Empty without labels.

nextStatuses.description: The statuses `changeIssueStatus` takes now (STATUS-1). Empty for a `CLOSED` issue.

overdue.description: The due date is before today in the installation time zone (`POPDESK_TIMEZONE`, S6A-AC-35). `false` without a due date. Judged by the server when it answers; show this instead of comparing with the browser's date.

reopenable.description: `reopenIssue` works now: the issue is `RESOLVED`, or `CLOSED` for less than 14 days (STATUS-4).

resolvedAt.description: When the issue became `RESOLVED`; null when it is not resolved (S3-AC-59).

sla.description: The SLA goals of the issue; null when it is not under SLA: it was filed while no SLA goal was set, and stays so whatever the policy becomes (S8A-AC-11, S8A-AC-30).

version.description: Goes up by 1 on every change to the issue (S0-AC-45). Not when popdesk works out its SLA due times again after a policy change; `sla` and `updatedAt` stay too (S8A-AC-21).

photoUpdatedAt.description: When the profile photo last changed; null without a photo (`getPhoto`) and for popdesk itself.

field.description: The field that changed: `STATUS`, `ASSIGNEE`, `TITLE`, `CONTENT`, `PRIORITY`, or `ATTACHMENT` (a file or content image was attached to the issue or one of its comments, or deleted; one entry for each attachment, S5-AC-40, S5-AC-41), `LABEL` (a label was put on or taken off; one entry for each label, S6A-AC-60), `DUE_DATE` (the due date was set, changed, or cleared, S6A-AC-61), or `LINK` (a link to another issue was made or removed; the same change is an entry of the other issue too, S6C-AC-20). A `LINK` entry whose other issue the caller cannot see is left out, also from the count of pages, and is back when the caller can see it again (S6C-AC-22). `TRASH`: the issue was deleted into the trash (new value `TRASHED`), restored from it (old value `TRASHED`, new value null), or purged (old value `TRASHED`, new value `PURGED`); the actor is the admin, or popdesk itself for a purge after 30 days (S7A-AC-06) and for a delete by automatic cleanup (`POPDESK_ISSUE_RETENTION`, S10B-AC-20). Later releases add names, so this is a plain string; show an entry with a name you do not know as a change without detail. Null for `CREATED`.

id.description: Entries of an issue are in the order of their IDs.

newLink.description: For `LINK`: the link that was made, like `oldLink`; null when one was removed. Null for every other field.

newPerson.description: For `ASSIGNEE`: the assignee after the change; null when it was cleared. Null for every other field.

newValue.description: The value after the change, like `oldValue`. For `ATTACHMENT`: the ID of the attachment that was attached; null when one was deleted. For `LABEL`: the name of the label that was put on; null when one was taken off. For `DUE_DATE`: the date after, `YYYY-MM-DD`; null when it was cleared. For `TRASH`: `TRASHED` on a delete, `PURGED` on a purge, null on a restore.

oldLink.description: For `LINK`: the link that was removed, seen from this issue, with the other issue's current key and title (S6C-AC-21); null when one was made. Null for every other field.

oldPerson.description: For `ASSIGNEE`: the assignee before the change, by the account's current name; null when there was none. Null for every other field.

oldValue.description: The value before the change: the name of the status or priority, or the title or content as it was. For `ATTACHMENT`: the ID of the attachment that was deleted, never its file name (S5-AC-43); null when one was attached. For `LABEL`: the name the label had when it was taken off, not changed by a later rename (S6A-AC-05); null when one was put on. For `DUE_DATE`: the date before, `YYYY-MM-DD`; null when there was none. Null for `CREATED`, for `ASSIGNEE`, for `LINK`, and when there was no value. For `TRASH`: `TRASHED` on a restore and a purge, null on a delete. `TITLE` and `CONTENT` entries of a purged issue have both values null (S7A-AC-30).

issue.description: The other issue, by its current key and title.

type.description: Seen from the issue whose history this is (S6C-AC-13).

items.description: Only links whose other issue the caller can see, in the order they were made (S6C-AC-12). A link the caller cannot see is left out and not counted anywhere; it is back when the caller can see the other issue again.

title.description: The title as it is now, not as it was when the item was made.

assigneeUnavailable.description: The assignee can no longer see the issue (ISSUE-11). `false` without an assignee.

filedOnBehalf.description: Staff filed the issue for the reporter (ISSUE-9).

labels.description: Labels of the issue, in name order whatever the case (S6A-AC-50). Empty without labels.

openTaskCount.description: Tasks of the issue that are `OPEN` and not deleted, also on a `CLOSED` issue (S6B-AC-70). 0 without tasks.

overdue.description: The due date is before today in the installation time zone (S6A-AC-35). `false` without a due date.

sla.description: The SLA goals of the issue; null when it is not under SLA (S8A-AC-30). The worse of the two running goals decides the `sla` filter (S8A-AC-31).

items.description: In the order they were made, deleted ones as traces in their place.

openCount.description: Tasks that are `OPEN` and not deleted, also on a `CLOSED` issue.

issueCount.description: Issues of the company that have this label now (S6A-AC-10).

name.description: 1 to 30 characters, unique in the company whatever the case.

enabled.description: `IMAP_HOST`, `IMAP_USER`, `IMAP_PASSWORD`, and `MAIL_INBOUND_ADDRESS` are all set, outside a sandbox.

lastFailure.description: The last of them; null without one.

lastSuccessAt.description: The end of the last round that succeeded: written once its emails (up to 100) are handled and moved, the alerts judged, and the daily mailbox cleanup done. Null before the first since the app started.

offReason.description: Why it is off: `NOT_SET` without the settings, `SANDBOX` in a sandbox even with them (S12-AC-03). Null when on.

quarantined90d.description: Emails quarantined in the last 90 days: failed five times, too large, too complex, or over the rate limit (`QUARANTINED` and `RATE_LIMITED`).

retrying.description: Emails left in the inbox folder to try again: a record with no outcome and at least one attempt.

roundFailures.description: Rounds that failed since the app started (S12-AC-10).

companies.description: The companies an agent is assigned to, in code order; `[]` for an admin, who sees every company.

locale.description: Language of the screens and of the account's email.

photoUpdatedAt.description: When the profile photo last changed; null without a photo (`getPhoto`).

invitationCancelled.description: The account never accepted its invitation and the invitation is cancelled (S1A-AC-42).

doneAt.description: When the task became `DONE`; null while it is `OPEN`.

overdue.description: The task is `OPEN` and its due date is before today in the installation time zone (S6B-AC-07).

actor.description: Who did it; null for an item about no issue, and null for what popdesk itself did, such as closing a `RESOLVED` issue after 7 days (S7A-AC-43).

commentId.description: The comment the item is about; null when it is about no comment.

companyCode.description: The company of the issue, or the company a `MEMBERSHIP_REQUESTED`, `COMPANY_EXPORT_READY`, or `COMPANY_EXPORT_FAILED` item is about; null for the other kinds.

issue.description: The issue the item is about, as it is now; null for `DELIVERY_FAILED`, `ATTACHMENT_QUOTA_WARNING`, `MAIL_STALLED`, `WEBHOOK_STALLED`, `AUDIT_FORWARD_STALLED`, `CLEANUP_STALLED`, `MAIL_IN_STALLED`, `MAIL_IN_QUARANTINED` (S12-AC-37), `MEMBERSHIP_REQUESTED` (S4-AC-40), `SLA_RECALCULATED` (S8B-AC-15), `COMPANY_EXPORT_READY`, `COMPANY_EXPORT_FAILED`, and `ISSUE_RETENTION_ARMED` (S10B-AC-27).

linkedIssue.description: For `LINKED_ISSUE_RESOLVED` and `LINKED_ISSUE_CLOSED`: the linked issue that was resolved or closed, with its key and title as they are now; `issue` is the caller's own issue it is linked to (S6C-AC-31). Such an item is listed only while the caller can see both issues (S6C-AC-33). Null for the other kinds (S6C-AC-34).

readAt.description: When the caller marked it read.

retentionCount.description: For `ISSUE_RETENTION_ARMED`: how many issues automatic cleanup would move to the trash when the item was written (S10B-AC-19). Null for the other kinds.

retentionDays.description: For `ISSUE_RETENTION_ARMED`: `POPDESK_ISSUE_RETENTION` in whole days, rounded down (S10B-AC-19). Null for the other kinds.

slaSummary.description: For `SLA_RECALCULATED`: how many issues working the SLA due times out again made overdue, due soon, or no longer either, counted as changes to an issue (S8B-AC-12). Null for the other kinds (S8B-AC-15).

task.description: The task a `TASK_ASSIGNED` item is about, with its title as it is now; null for the other kinds (S6B-AC-33). Deleting the task deletes its items (S6B-AC-36).

photoUpdatedAt.description: When the profile photo last changed; null without a photo (`getPhoto`).

title.description: The title as it is now, not as it was when the item was made (INBOX-1).
The title as it is now, not as it was when the item was made.

apps.description: The apps OIDC sign-in is on for, `CONSOLE` before `PORTAL`; empty when off.

lastSuccessAt.description: The last OIDC sign-in that started a session; null before the first since the app started.

providerFailures.description: Provider-side failures since the app started: discovery, token exchange, ID token checks.

issues.description: Issues that are not `CLOSED` and have this account as assignee.

tasks.description: Tasks that are `OPEN`, not deleted, on issues that are not `CLOSED`, and have this account as assignee; for an agent taken off a company, only tasks of that company's issues (S6B-AC-75).

resetLink.description: The reset link, only when SMTP is not configured; shown once, the token is in the fragment after `#`. `null` when the reset email is sent.

cancelled.description: An admin cancelled the invitation; the link does not work until it is sent again (S1A-AC-42).

companies.description: The companies a customer was invited to; `[]` for staff.

expired.description: The current link is past its 7 days.

name.description: The name the manager typed. The account's own name is in `account`.

photoUpdatedAt.description: When the profile photo last changed; null without a photo (`getPhoto`).

colors.description: The values made from the accent color; null without one, and the app's own colors apply.

displayName.description: 1 to 50 characters; `popdesk` until an admin changes it (S9-AC-05).

dark.description: The same for the dark theme; null without a logo.

light.description: `/api/public/branding/logos/{theme}?v={fingerprint}` for the light theme; null without a logo.

email.description: Leading and trailing whitespace and case are ignored.

password.description: 10 to 72 characters, not only whitespace, not the same as the email (AUTH-5).

token.description: The token from the reset link's fragment (after `#`). Sent only in the body.

accountId.description: An `ACTIVE` admin, or an `ACTIVE` agent assigned to the issue's company (ISSUE-7).

dueDate.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, today or later in the installation time zone (`POPDESK_TIMEZONE`, S6A-AC-30, S6A-AC-34). A time, an offset, or a day that does not exist (`2026-02-30`) is not taken (S6A-AC-31).

oidc.description: OIDC sign-in is on for this host's app (`OIDC_APPS`): the sign-in page offers it.

email.description: Leading and trailing whitespace and case are ignored.

dueAt.description: When the goal runs out, to the second. Still given after `MET` or `MISSED`, as it was when the clock stopped. Null without a goal.

remainingMinutes.description: Business minutes left while the clock runs, rounded down; after `dueAt` a negative number of business minutes past it, rounded up (S8A-AC-19). Null while the clock is stopped and without a goal.

state.description: `MET` or `MISSED` once the clock stopped for good; otherwise `BREACHED` after `dueAt`, `WARNING` from 80% of the goal on, `OK` before that. At `dueAt` itself the goal is not breached yet. Null when the issue's priority has no such goal (S8A-AC-10).

medianMinutes.description: The lower median of the business time the counted issues took, in minutes rounded down: of an even number of values, the smaller of the middle two. For first response only issues stopped by a response count here; issues resolved or closed without one count only in `met` and `missed`. Null when there is nothing to take the median of (S8B-AC-24).

missed.description: Issues whose goal stopped as `MISSED`. Issues without a goal (`NONE`) are in neither count.

closes.description: `HH:MM`, later than `opens`; `24:00` is the end of the day. A span never goes past midnight. Null, together with `opens`, on a day without business hours.

opens.description: `HH:MM`, from `00:00` to `23:59`, in whole minutes. Null, together with `closes`, on a day without business hours.

changedBy.description: The admin who made this version; null when popdesk made it: version 1, and a version made because the time zone changed (S8A-AC-07).

holidays.description: Days that count no business time, even when every day counts 24 hours: `YYYY-MM-DD` in the installation time zone, earliest first, at most 500 (S8A-AC-12).

hours.description: Seven items, one for each weekday, from `MONDAY` to `SUNDAY`. When no day has business hours, every day counts all 24 hours; otherwise a day without them counts none (S8A-AC-12).

targets.description: Four items, one for each priority, from `LOW` to `URGENT`.

timeZone.description: The time zone the business hours and holidays are read in: the installation's `POPDESK_TIMEZONE`, for example `Asia/Seoul`. Set by popdesk, not by this endpoint; when the setting changes, popdesk makes a new version within a minute (S8A-AC-07).

version.description: Goes up by 1 when the goals, the business hours, the holidays, or the time zone change (SLA-1). Send it back with `updateSlaPolicy`.

becameWarning.description: Issues that became `WARNING` from `OK` or from having no goal; 0 or more.

released.description: Issues that moved back from `BREACHED` or `WARNING`, losing their goal included; 0 or more.

firstResponseMinutes.description: Business minutes from filing to the first public comment of staff, 1 to 525,600 (365 days of 24 hours); null without this goal (S8A-AC-01).

resolutionMinutes.description: Business minutes from filing to `RESOLVED` or `CLOSED`, 1 to 525,600; not shorter than `firstResponseMinutes` when both are set. Null without this goal (S8A-AC-01, S8A-AC-04).

anonymized.description: The account was anonymized (PII-4): `name` and `email` are the anonymous values, `status` is `SUSPENDED`, and nothing brings it back (S10A-AC-13).

oidcLinked.description: The account is linked to an OIDC provider's account (AUTH-6, S11-AC-26): later OIDC sign-ins match it by that link only. `unlinkAccountOidc` removes it.

photoUpdatedAt.description: When the profile photo last changed; null without a photo (`getPhoto`).

cleanupJobs.description: Every cleanup job, in name order (S4B-AC-30).

oidc.description: OIDC sign-in, counted since the app started (S11-AC-30).

sandbox.description: `POPDESK_SANDBOX=true`: the webhook and the outside copy of the audit log are off, and email goes to one address only or is off (S4B-AC-08).

sandboxMailToSet.description: The sandbox has an address to send email to (`POPDESK_SANDBOX_MAIL_TO`). `false` outside a sandbox. The address itself is never given.

assignee.description: Null when nobody is assigned, and once the task is deleted.

doneAt.description: When the task became `DONE`; null while it is `OPEN` (S6B-AC-06).

doneBy.description: Who made the task `DONE`; null while it is `OPEN` (S6B-AC-06).

dueDate.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`; null without a due date, and once the task is deleted (TASK-6).

id.description: Tasks of an issue are in the order of their IDs, the order they were made (S6B-AC-24).

notes.description: Notes and changes, oldest first (S6B-AC-24). Empty once the task is deleted (S6B-AC-10).

overdue.description: The task is `OPEN` and its due date is before today in the installation time zone (S6B-AC-07). `false` for a `DONE` task, without a due date, and once the task is deleted.

title.description: 1 to 100 characters. An empty string once the task is deleted (S6B-AC-10).
The title as it is now.

author.description: Who wrote the note, or who made the change.

content.description: The note as written: plain text, 1 to 4,000 characters; line breaks are kept. An empty string once the note is deleted (S6B-AC-22), and always for `CHANGE`.

deleted.description: The note was deleted (S6B-AC-22). Always `false` for `CHANGE`.

editedAt.description: When the author last changed the note; null when it never changed (S6B-AC-21). Always null for `CHANGE`.

field.description: For `CHANGE`: the field that changed, `STATUS`, `ASSIGNEE`, `DUE_DATE`, or `TITLE` (S6B-AC-30). Later releases may add names, so this is a plain string; show an entry with a name you do not know as a change without detail. Null for `NOTE`.

id.description: Entries of a task are in the order of their IDs (S6B-AC-24).

newPerson.description: For `ASSIGNEE`: the assignee after; null when it was cleared. Null for every other field.

newValue.description: For `CHANGE`, the value after, like `oldValue`. Null when the value was cleared.

oldPerson.description: For `ASSIGNEE`: the assignee before, by the account's current name; null when there was none. Null for every other field.

oldValue.description: For `CHANGE`, the value before: for `STATUS` the status name, for `DUE_DATE` the date `YYYY-MM-DD`, for `TITLE` the title as it was. Null for `ASSIGNEE`, for `NOTE`, and when there was no value.

content.description: Plain text, 1 to 4,000 characters; only whitespace is refused (S6B-AC-20). Line breaks are kept.

id.description: The ID to write as `attachment:{id}` and to send in `imageIds`. Hard to guess, but not a permission check (ATT-7). It stays the attachment's ID once the image is attached.

errorKind.description: Kind of the error, for example `SMTP_AUTHENTICATION_FAILED` or `CONNECTION_FAILED`, as in `FailedDelivery.lastErrorKind`, or `RATE_LIMITED` when the address already got its 50 emails this hour; null when `ok`.

ok.description: The SMTP server took the email.

serverReply.description: What the SMTP server answered, as plain text of up to 500 characters, with line breaks but no other control characters; show it as text, never as markup. The address the email went to is masked after its first character, and the SMTP user name and password are replaced by `***`. null when the server gave no answer: when the email was taken, or when the server could not be reached.

accent.description: Text, links, and the main button.

accentHover.description: The main button under the pointer.

accentSubtle.description: A light background of the accent, for example the chosen row.

onAccent.description: Text on `accent`: the theme's background color.

deletedBy.description: The admin who deleted the issue, by the account's current name. null: automatic cleanup (PII-6) moved it here, because it was closed longer ago than `POPDESK_ISSUE_RETENTION` (S10B-AC-20, S10B-AC-22).

purgeAt.description: When popdesk purges the issue by itself: `deletedAt` plus 30 days, measured in UTC (S7A-AC-31). The hourly job may do it up to an hour later.

status.description: The status the issue had when it was deleted; the trash does not change it.

title.description: The title as it was when the issue was deleted.

accent.description: `#RRGGBB`, either letter case, kept in capitals; null for the app's own colors (S9-AC-10, S9-AC-11).

displayName.description: 1 to 50 characters after trimming and NFC; no line breaks, control characters, or direction marks (S9-AC-09).

version.description: The `version` of the branding as the caller read it (S9-AC-08).

imageIds.description: IDs of temporary images the caller uploaded with `uploadImage`, up to 20. The save attaches them to the issue, and to the comment when it writes one, or attaches none of them and saves nothing (S5-AC-20). Only these IDs are attached: the server does not look for `attachment:{id}` in the content, and an ID the content does not name is attached too (S5-AC-25). An ID given twice counts once. Left out, `null`, or empty: nothing is attached.

mentions.description: The whole list of account IDs the comment mentions from now on, up to 10 counting the whole list. Only an account new to the list is checked by the rules of `createComment`; one the comment mentions already is not checked again and may stay. `null` is the same as an empty list. Left out, the mentions stay (S4-AC-24).

content.description: Markdown, up to 10,000 characters. `null` clears it.

imageIds.description: IDs of temporary images the caller uploaded with `uploadImage`, up to 20. The save attaches them to the issue, and to the comment when it writes one, or attaches none of them and saves nothing (S5-AC-20). Only these IDs are attached: the server does not look for `attachment:{id}` in the content, and an ID the content does not name is attached too (S5-AC-25). An ID given twice counts once. Left out, `null`, or empty: nothing is attached.

title.description: 1 to 200 characters after trimming. `null` is refused.

version.description: The `version` of the issue as the caller read it (S3-AC-19).

color.description: `#` and six hexadecimal digits, as for `createLabel`.

name.description: 1 to 30 characters, as for `createLabel`. Changing only the case of the label's own name works (S6A-AC-03).

locale.description: Language of the account's email. The screens are in Korean for now.

assigneeId.description: An `ACTIVE` admin, or an `ACTIVE` agent assigned to the issue's company (TASK-6). Checked only when it differs from the current assignee (S6B-AC-04). `null` clears it.

dueDate.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, today or later in the installation time zone (S6B-AC-05). `null` clears it.

status.description: `DONE` records who and when; `OPEN` clears both (S6B-AC-06). `null` is refused.

title.description: 1 to 100 characters after the whitespace around it is removed. `null` is refused.

post.description: Cannot be undone (PII-4). The name becomes the anonymous name in the installation's language (`POPDESK_LOCALE`), the email `deleted-{id}@invalid`, and the status `SUSPENDED`; an `INVITED` account too (S10A-AC-08). In the same transaction it ends every session of the account and removes its profile photo, password, sign-in lock, invitation and password reset tokens, queued emails to it, and its inbox items (S10A-AC-09), puts the anonymous values into its membership requests (S10A-AC-10) and into its audit entries, and computes the audit chain again from the first changed entry (S10A-AC-17, S10A-AC-18). What it wrote stays, shown with the anonymous name (S10A-AC-11). Its old email can be invited again as a new account (S10A-AC-15). Recorded as `AUDIT_RECHAINED` and then `ACCOUNT_ANONYMIZED` (S10A-AC-16). Issues keep the account as assignee, marked `assigneeUnavailable`, unless `clearAssignments` is sent (S10A-AC-14).

parameters.description: `true`: in the same request, also clear the assignee of every issue counted by `countOpenAssignments` (S3-AC-69). Each of them gets a history entry by the caller, and no webhook message is sent (S3-AC-70). Left out or `false`, assignees stay.

Run the integrity check. Nothing changed.

post.description: Computes every hash again from the start of the chain, or from the kept starting point when old entries were removed by the retention period (S1B-AC-14, S1B-AC-17). A broken chain is a 200 with `valid` false: `ENTRY_MISMATCH` names the first entry that does not hold (a changed entry, or the entry after a removed one), `HEAD_MISMATCH` means the last entries were removed (S1B-AC-15, S1B-AC-16, S1B-AC-42). A valid result does not rule out that the whole chain was written again. One check runs at a time.

get.description: The display name, the accent color as saved, the values made from it and their contrast, and the logo of each theme (S9-AC-06). Checks, in this order: role (403).

put.description: Saves both and makes the next version (S9-AC-07). Sending what the branding has already is 200 with the branding as it is, no new version, and no audit entry. A change leaves an audit entry `BRANDING_CHANGED` with the target `{"type": "BRANDING"}` and, in `changes`, `displayName` or `accent` from before to after for each that changed; an accent is its `#RRGGBB` or null (S9-AC-20). Logos are not touched. Checks, in this order: role (403), the body (400), `version` (409), so a body that is wrong is 400 even with an old version (S9-AC-08).

put.description: Takes a PNG, JPEG, or WebP file of up to 512 KB, judged by its content, never SVG. popdesk turns it by its EXIF orientation, scales it to fit 512 by 128 px (never larger), and keeps only that copy as a PNG without metadata, not the uploaded file (S9-AC-15). The new logo replaces the theme's logo; the branding's `version` stays (S9-AC-18). `PUT`, unlike a profile photo's `POST`: each theme has one logo, put in place. A new logo leaves an audit entry `BRANDING_LOGO_CHANGED` with the target `{"type": "BRANDING", "theme": "LIGHT"}` (or `DARK`) and, in `changes`, `logo` from the fingerprint before, or null, to the new one; the same file again leaves none (S9-AC-21). Checks, in this order: role (403), the `file` part (400, looked for before anything else in the request), rate limit (429, refused uploads count too), `theme` (404), the size of the file (413), a place for decoding (503, profile photos and logos together), then the file's first bytes and pixel count (400); a refused file leaves the logo as it was (S9-AC-16).

Checks, in this order: role (403), the body (400), `version` (409).

200.description: The policy as it is now.

400.description: `INVALID_INPUT`, nothing changed (S8A-AC-04); `fields` lists all, named with the place in the list, for example `targets[2].resolutionMinutes`: a goal out of 1 to 525,600 (`targets[i].firstResponseMinutes` or `targets[i].resolutionMinutes`, `OUT_OF_RANGE`); a resolution goal shorter than the first response goal (`targets[i].resolutionMinutes`, `OUT_OF_RANGE`); priorities not the four, one twice, or one unknown (`targets`, `UNKNOWN_VALUE`); weekdays not the seven, one twice, or one unknown (`hours`, `UNKNOWN_VALUE`); only one of `opens` and `closes` (the empty one, `hours[i].opens` or `hours[i].closes`, `REQUIRED`); a time not `HH:MM` in whole minutes, or `24:00` in `opens` (`hours[i].opens` or `hours[i].closes`, `INVALID_FORMAT`); `closes` not later than `opens` (`hours[i].closes`, `OUT_OF_RANGE`); over 500 holidays (`holidays`, `TOO_MANY`); a day twice (`holidays[i]`, the later one, `UNKNOWN_VALUE`); `version` missing (`version`, `REQUIRED`).

409.description: `VERSION_CONFLICT`: `version` is not the policy's current one, for example because another admin saved first. This is 409 even when the values sent are the ones the policy has now. Nothing changed. Read the policy again (S8A-AC-03).

get.description: One item for each company the caller can see: every company for admins, assigned ones for agents (S7B-AC-03). A company the caller is not assigned to has no item, and its issues are in no count. Companies of every status are listed, archived ones too, and a company without issues has an item with zeros (S7B-AC-01). Issues in the trash and purged ones are not counted; private issues are (S7B-AC-02). Ordered by `open`, the most first, then by `companyCode` (S7B-AC-04). Not paged: every item at once. While the SLA policy is on, each item has the SLA goals of its issues over the last `days` (S8B-AC-22).

parameters.description: The SLA columns count goals that stopped within the last `days` × 24 hours: 7, 30, or 90 (S8B-AC-21, S8B-AC-23). The issue counts are as they are now whatever it is.

200.description: The counts as they are now.

400.description: `INVALID_INPUT`: `days` is not 7, 30, or 90 (`UNKNOWN_VALUE`), or not a number (`INVALID_FORMAT`).

parameters.description: Page number, from 1.

400.description: `INVALID_INPUT`: `page` or `size` out of range (`OUT_OF_RANGE`).

post.description: Puts a `failed` row of any channel back in the queue with its attempts and failure times cleared; it is sent at once and, when it fails again, retried like a new row (S4B-AC-14, S4B-AC-16). The checks before sending run again, so an email whose recipient may no longer get it is dropped, not sent (S4B-AC-15). A row that is back in the queue already is 204 too and changes nothing (S4B-AC-18). Leaves an audit entry `DELIVERY_RESENT` when it changed the row (S4B-AC-20).

400.description: `CHANNEL_DISABLED`: the row's channel is not configured or the sandbox turned it off. The row stays as it is (S4B-AC-17).

404.description: `NOT_FOUND`: no such row. It was sent, dropped, or cleaned up 7 days after it failed (S4B-AC-18).

get.description: For mail, webhook, and the outside copy of the audit log (`auditForward`): configured or not, last success, queued and failed rows (S0-AC-81, S1B-AC-33). The console also reads `mail.enabled` to decide whether to offer invitation links (C-10). In a sandbox the webhook and the outside copy are not `enabled`, and neither is mail without a sandbox address (S4B-AC-08). Each cleanup job comes with its last run (S4B-AC-30). `oidc` is OIDC sign-in, counted in memory since the app started (S11-AC-30). `mailIn` is receiving email over IMAP: rounds counted in memory, retried and quarantined emails from the records (S12-AC-36). No SMTP password, webhook URL, or address or token of the outside copy, no OIDC issuer, client ID, or secret, and no IMAP host, user, password, or folder (S4B-AC-31).
get.summary: Outgoing channels, the sandbox, and cleanup jobs

post.description: Sends one email to the caller's own address, in a sandbox to the sandbox address, within the request and without the outbox, and says what the SMTP server answered (S4B-AC-22). A server that refuses or cannot be reached is 200 with `ok` false, never a 5xx (S4B-AC-23). The email counts toward the 50 an hour one address gets (S4B-AC-13). Leaves an audit entry `TEST_MAIL_SENT` whether it worked or not (S4B-AC-27). The request can take as long as the SMTP timeouts.

200.description: The email was tried; `ok` says whether it went.

400.description: `CHANNEL_DISABLED`: email is not configured, or this is a sandbox without an address (S4B-AC-25).

429.description: `RATE_LIMITED`: more than 5 test emails in 60 seconds (S4B-AC-26). Counted before the channel is checked.

get.description: Every deleted issue that is not purged yet, of every company, the latest deleted first; issues deleted at the same moment by key, the highest number first (S7A-AC-20). Checks, in this order: role (403), `page` and `size` (400).

delete.description: At once, without waiting for the 30 days (S7A-AC-30). What was written is deleted: the title and content (left empty), comments and mentions, attachments and their files, tasks and their notes, links, labels on the issue, its inbox items, its waiting messages, and the `Idempotency-Key` of its filing; the title and content values of its history entries are cleared. The key, company, status, times, and history entries stay, but the issue is shown nowhere again and its number is not used again (S7A-AC-32, S7A-AC-35). Leaves a history entry `TRASH` from `TRASHED` to `PURGED` (S7A-AC-06) and an audit entry `ISSUE_PURGED` (S7A-AC-07). Checks, in this order: role (403), the issue in the trash (404).

post.description: The issue is back as it was before it was deleted: its content, comments, attachments, tasks and their notes, links, labels, assignee, due date, and status, and its inbox items are listed again (S7A-AC-21). What was not sent while it was in the trash is not sent now (S7A-AC-10). A `RESOLVED` issue is closed by popdesk 7 days after the restore, not after `resolvedAt`, which stays as it was (S7A-AC-22). Goes up `version` by 1 and leaves a history entry `TRASH` with the old value `TRASHED` (S7A-AC-06) and an audit entry `ISSUE_RESTORED` (S7A-AC-07). Takes no body. Checks, in this order: role (403), the issue in the trash (404), its links (409).

200.description: The issue as it is now.

404.description: `NOT_FOUND`: no issue with this key is in the trash: no such issue, an issue that is not deleted, or one that is purged already, for example by someone else just before (S7A-AC-23). One body for all of these.

Otherwise to the sign-in page of the host's app: `/login?oidc=failed` (the sign-in cannot go on, one value whatever the reason), `/login?oidc=unavailable` (the provider could not be reached or answered wrongly), `/login?oidc=busy` (too many sign-ins started) (S11-AC-11, S11-AC-13, S11-AC-17).
